## Source: amazon-inspector (fe5161ec5e3bb6bc18d6975809d09281190c49b41a4f926dfa6a28cabf061e04)
claims-acct-unlock@25.2.1 ships no source code; package.json declares a single dependency 'node-acct-utilssss21' resolved from a bare HTTPS tarball URL on an unrelated GitHub user's repository (github.com/GamerD11/ping_test) at the mutable branch ref refs/heads/main, with no commit pin and no integrity hash. On npm install, npm fetches whatever bytes are currently served at that URL and installs them as a dependency, running any lifecycle scripts bundled inside. The repository owner can replace the tarball contents at any time without any change to this package. The dependency name does not correspond to a known library and resembles a typo of an internal/utility package, consistent with a dependency-confusion / lure shape where the manifest itself is the entire attack surface.

## Source: ossf-package-analysis (49e97601227bdd6c1f90001323f6ec7ec7242416e3577d752dd5045453688a14)
The OpenSSF Package Analysis project identified 'claims-acct-unlock' @ 25.2.1 (npm) as malicious.

It is considered malicious because:

- The package communicates with a domain associated with malicious activity.

- The package executes one or more commands associated with malicious behavior.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
